A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

Merlin is required for proper synaptogenesis in cerebellar neurons, which is paralleled by an increase of excitatory neurotransmitter release and a decrease in the frequency of miniature postsynptic currents.
Merlin is required to maintain proper synaptic organization of PCs and GCs in the cerebellar cortex and to regulate synaptic plasticity in the cerebellomotor circuit.
Merlin is involved in the regulation of cytoskeletal dynamics and synapse formation and function in cerebellar neurons, which may be of importance for the development of NF2-associated tumors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Merlin has distinct roles in cerebellar synapse development depending on the cell type in which it is expressed.
Merlin is required for the development of a functional cerebellar circuit.
Merlin modulates process out- and synaptogenesis, which may be relevant for NF2-associated brain tumors and for the understanding of the role of Merlin in the CNS.
